summary.short: Amends the federal civil remedy for intimate images (15 U.S.C. 6851) so that identifiable individuals can sue persons who knowingly produce, possess, disclose or solicit non-consensual intimate digital forgeries in U.S. district courts. The text ends with a Senate passage date of January 13, 2026.
summary.long: The bill amends Section 1309 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2022 (15 U.S.C. 6851). It defines an intimate digital forgery as an intimate visual depiction of an identifiable individual that falsely represents the individual or the intimate conduct, is created by software, machine learning, artificial intelligence or other computer-generated means, and is indistinguishable from an authentic depiction to a reasonable person; labels or disclosure do not change this status. Identifiable individuals may sue in federal district court persons who knowingly produce or possess a forgery with intent to disclose it, disclose it, or solicit or receive it without consent, and persons who knowingly produce a forgery where the individual was harmed or reasonably likely to be harmed, where the conduct affects interstate or foreign commerce. Relief includes liquidated damages of $150,000, or $250,000 in specified aggravated cases, or actual damages including defendant profits; punitive damages; injunctions; and privacy-protective orders. Actions must be filed within 10 years of the later of discovery or age 18. Sec. 3(c) preserves other federal, state and tribal law and allows at-least-as-protective state laws; Sec. 4 provides severability and states the Act does not limit or expand intellectual property law. No effective date is stated.
